_about: Master timeline for the Miami 3D timelapse, 500 BC to 2026. year: integer (negative = BC). category: war | disaster | structure | land | arrival | civic | unrest | demolition. war_ref points to data/war_sequences.json. Coordinates are approximate (WGS84) for scene placement. confidence: high / medium / disputed (see README).

events.title: The Miami Circle
events.summary: Tequesta/Glades-culture site at the mouth of the Miami River: a 38 ft (11.5 m) circle of about 600 postholes and 24 basins cut into limestone bedrock; dated roughly 500 BC to AD 750 (other estimates: 1,700-2,000 years old). The only known prehistoric structure cut into bedrock in the eastern US.

location.name: Brickell Point, south bank of the river mouth

events.visual: Circle of posts with a thatched structure; huts along both river banks; canoes

events.title: Ponce de Leon sails into Biscayne Bay
events.summary: Juan Ponce de Leon reaches the bay he calls 'Chequescha' (a form of Tequesta). The first European to visit the Miami area.
events.visual: Spanish ships on the horizon, passing

events.title: Menendez, the mission and its failure
events.summary: 1566 landing; March 1567 stockade mission with 30 soldiers and Brother Francisco Villareal; conflict after soldiers kill the chief's uncle; mission abandoned 1570.

events.title: Raids and removal to Cuba
events.summary: Carolina and Yamasee raids depopulate the peninsula (by 1707). 280 natives taken to Cuba in 1710; nearly 200 die.

events.title: Last Spanish mission and stockade
events.summary: Jesuits Monaco and Alana build a stockade; only 180 natives remain; abandoned within months.

events.title: The last natives leave; Florida becomes British
events.summary: Spain cedes Florida to Britain; the remaining South Florida natives are evacuated to Cuba. Numbers for the Miami area specifically are not recorded (80 families of Calusa is a figure for the southwest coast).
events.visual: Village empties; population counter drops toward zero

events.title: British land grant
events.summary: Samuel Touchett receives a 20,000-acre grant in the Miami area (surveyed by Bernard Romans in 1772). Bahamian settlers ('squatters') arrive from the 1790s; first permanent European settlers around 1800.

events.title: Cape Florida Lighthouse
events.summary: 65 ft brick tower built on the south tip of Key Biscayne.

events.title: Fitzpatrick plantation
events.summary: Richard Fitzpatrick buys land on the Miami River from James Egan and runs a sugar and citrus plantation worked by about 60 enslaved people.

location.name: North bank of the Miami River

events.title: Hurricane floods Key Biscayne
events.summary: A major hurricane damages the lighthouse and keeper's house and leaves the island under three feet of water.

events.title: Second Seminole War: plantation evacuated
events.summary: The Miami River plantation is evacuated under threat of Seminole attack.

events.title: Seminoles attack Cape Florida Lighthouse
events.summary: Tower set alight; Aaron Carter killed; John Thompson rescued by the Navy the next day. The light stays dark until 1847.

events.title: Fort Dallas built
events.summary: Navy Lt. L. M. Powell builds blockhouses at the river mouth; Army garrison Oct 1839 to Jan 1842.

events.title: Harney's canoe raid
events.summary: 90 men in 16 canoes leave Fort Dallas for the Everglades; Chakaika killed; back after 12 days.

events.title: Village of Miami platted
events.summary: Second Seminole War ends. William English gets title from his uncle Fitzpatrick (land purchase dated May 20, 1843: 2,660 acres on both banks), re-establishes the plantation and plats a 'Village of Miami' on the south bank that never materialised. Miami becomes the Dade County seat in 1844.

location.name: South bank of the Miami River

events.title: Stone slave quarters / later Fort Dallas barracks
events.summary: Oolitic limestone building built on the English plantation as slave quarters; later used as Army barracks; moved in sections to Lummus Park in 1924.

location.name: Original site, north bank near the river mouth

events.title: Lighthouse relit
events.summary: Rebuilt Cape Florida light relit with 17 Argand lamps. In 1855 the tower is raised to 95 ft with a second-order Fresnel lens (relit March 1856).

events.title: Fort Dallas regarrisoned; Third Seminole War
events.summary: Troops return Oct 20, 1849; the fort is reestablished 1855-1858.

events.title: 96 residents
events.summary: The census reports ninety-six residents in the Miami area.

events.title: Civil War: the lighthouse is darkened
events.summary: Confederate sympathizers wreck the Cape Florida lamp and lens; Union blockade; the light is repaired in 1866.

events.title: The Brickells and the Lums
events.summary: William Brickell buys land on the south bank of the river (trading post). Henry and Charles Lum buy Miami Beach land for 75 cents an acre (coconut plantation attempts in the 1880s).

events.title: Biscayne House of Refuge
events.summary: US Life-Saving Service station on the barrier island (Miami Beach).

events.title: Cape Florida light decommissioned
events.summary: Replaced by the Fowey Rocks lighthouse offshore.

events.title: Coconut Grove settles
events.summary: Peacock Inn, the first hotel, in Coconut Grove (1884); Ralph Munroe's home on the bay (1886); Bahamian workers build the village.

events.title: Julia Tuttle arrives
events.summary: Buys 640 acres on the north bank of the Miami River and lives in the old Fort Dallas buildings.

events.title: The Great Freeze
events.summary: Freezes (Dec 1894, Feb 7 1895) destroy north Florida's citrus. Flagler agrees to extend his railroad to Miami (announced June 21, 1895; contract Oct 24, 1895).

events.title: The railroad arrives
events.summary: Tracks reach Miami April 7; first train April 13; scheduled service April 15. Flagler's men dredge a 9 ft channel at the river mouth; the spoil creates what becomes Brickell Key.

events.title: City of Miami incorporated
events.summary: Incorporation meeting at 2 p.m. above 'The Lobby' pool hall. Commonly cited: 368 registered voters, 162 of them Black workers (Wikipedia gives 502 voters incl. 100 Black; disputed).

events.title: Royal Palm Hotel opens
events.summary: Flagler's hotel on the north bank at the river mouth: 5 storeys plus a 6th-floor salon, 450 rooms; Miami's first electric lights, elevators and swimming pool. Built on the site of a Native American village.

events.title: Spanish-American War: Fort Brickell and Camp Miami
events.summary: Fort begun April 5; 7,000+ volunteers camp from June 24; war ends Aug 12 with no combat.

events.title: Government Cut
events.summary: Shipping channel dredged through the south end of the barrier island, separating Fisher Island from Miami Beach (dredging 1905-1911).

events.title: Draining the Everglades begins
events.summary: Canals begin to drain the Everglades.

events.title: Miami Canal dug; rapids destroyed
events.summary: The Miami River rapids (a 6 ft drop over 400-500 ft, about 4 miles from the mouth) are bypassed and removed. When the canal opens in March 1912, muck and ground rock silt the river, which must be dredged three times in two years.

location.name: Former rapids, North Fork of the Miami River

events.title: Collins Bridge
events.summary: 2.5-mile wooden toll bridge to Miami Beach, the longest wooden bridge in the world at the time. Carl Fisher arrives and dredges the bay to turn mangroves into land.

events.title: Vizcaya
events.summary: James Deering's estate: main house done by winter 1916, gardens into 1922-23.

events.title: Miami Beach chartered
events.summary: Town of Miami Beach chartered; becomes a city in 1917. Population 644 in 1920.

events.title: County Causeway
events.summary: Built from 1917, completed 1920; renamed MacArthur Causeway in 1942.

events.title: Islands dredged out of the bay
events.summary: Star, Palm, the Hibiscus and Sunset Islands, much of Normandy Isle and all of the Venetian Islands except Belle Isle are built from dredge fill. Bayfront Park is filled from 1924 and opens in March 1925. Haulover Cut opens in April 1925, making Miami Beach an island.

events.title: Land boom peak: the Miami News Tower (Freedom Tower)
events.summary: 289 ft tower, briefly the tallest in the South. The University of Miami is founded; Coral Gables and Hialeah incorporate; Coconut Grove and others are annexed.

events.title: Prinz Valdemar capsizes
events.summary: A 241 ft steel schooner overturns in the harbor channel. The port is closed for more than a month: about 100 ships wait offshore, 32 are trapped inside.

events.title: Biltmore Hotel
events.summary: Opens in Coral Gables; 315 ft, Florida's tallest until 1928. The Venetian Causeway also opens in 1926.

events.title: The Great Miami Hurricane
events.summary: Category 4 (145 mph), landfall near Perrine; 930 mb. Surge 14-15 ft in Coconut Grove; the County Causeway under 6 ft of water. 372-539+ dead; about 43,000 homeless. The 18-storey Meyer-Kiser Building is badly damaged. The boom ends.
events.visual: Four-beat 'siege': storm arrives from the SE, a calm eye (people went outside during the lull and were caught when the winds returned), surge floods the bayfront, rebuilding

events.title: Dade County Courthouse
events.summary: 360 ft, 28 storeys; the tallest building in Miami for 44 years.

events.title: Pan Am's 36th Street Airport
events.summary: Opens January 1929 (origin of today's Miami International Airport). Pan Am's Dinner Key seaplane terminal is dedicated March 25, 1934 (now Miami City Hall).

events.title: Royal Palm Hotel torn down
events.summary: Damaged by the 1926 hurricane and termites; condemned and demolished.

events.title: Assassination attempt on FDR
events.summary: In Bayfront Park, Giuseppe Zangara fires at President-elect Roosevelt; Chicago mayor Anton Cermak is fatally shot and four others are wounded.

events.title: Art Deco Miami Beach
events.summary: Art Deco hotels rise along Ocean Drive.

events.title: Orange Bowl stadium
events.summary: Stadium opens (demolished 2008). Liberty Square public housing also opens in 1937.

events.title: World War II
events.summary: Training city, dim-out, U-boat sinkings within sight of Miami Beach, blimp convoys.

events.title: Homestead hurricane; blimp base burns
events.summary: 170 mph winds; fire destroys NAS Richmond's three hangars with 25 blimps and 368 aircraft; 26 deaths overall.

events.title: Rickenbacker Causeway
events.summary: Road to Key Biscayne opens.

events.title: Hurricane King
events.summary: A small but intense hurricane whose eye passes directly over downtown Miami (gusts estimated at 150 mph); 20,861 houses damaged, 248 destroyed; surge only 3.4 ft.

events.title: Fontainebleau Hotel
events.summary: Opens on Miami Beach.

events.title: Cuban Revolution; the exile begins
events.summary: Castro takes power. Miami International Airport is dedicated; Julia Tuttle Causeway opens Dec 12, 1959 (I-195 complete Dec 22, 1961). 1960-62: Operation Pedro Pan brings over 14,000 unaccompanied Cuban children.

events.title: Bay of Pigs and JM/WAVE
events.summary: Fake 'defector' B-26 lands at MIA on April 15, 1961; the CIA's JM/WAVE secret war runs from South Miami-Dade.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.summary: 181+ F-100s and 10,000+ troops at Homestead; HAWK and later Nike Hercules batteries ring Miami until 1979. No shots fired.

events.title: Freedom Tower becomes 'El Refugio'
events.summary: The Cuban Assistance Center, called 'the Ellis Island of the South'.

events.title: JFK at the Orange Bowl
events.summary: Kennedy receives the flag of Brigade 2506 from the ransomed survivors.

events.title: Miami Marine Stadium
events.summary: Powerboat-racing stadium on Virginia Key; abandoned after Hurricane Andrew (1992).

events.title: Port moves to Dodge Island
events.summary: Port operations leave the Biscayne Boulevard waterfront for the new artificial island port.

events.title: Freedom Flights
events.summary: Twice-daily flights from Dec 1, 1965 to Apr 6, 1973 bring close to 300,000 Cubans. Hurricane Betsy (Sept 1965) floods Miami with the highest tides since 1926.

events.title: I-95 cuts through Overtown
events.summary: Interstate construction displaces about 12,000 Overtown residents (another figure: 8,500 households by 1968). The Dolphin Expressway opens in 1969.

events.title: 1968 Liberty City riot
events.summary: During the Republican National Convention in Miami Beach; 3 deaths.

events.title: One Biscayne Tower
events.summary: Takes the 'tallest in Miami' title from the Courthouse after 44 years. The Democratic and Republican conventions are both held in Miami Beach.

events.title: Art Deco District listed
events.summary: Miami Beach's Art Deco Historic District is added to the National Register.

events.title: Mariel boatlift
events.summary: About 125,000 Cubans in about 1,700 boats (Apr 15 to Oct 31); Orange Bowl refuge and tent city under I-95.

events.title: 1980 riots
events.summary: After the McDuffie verdict: 18 killed, over $100M damage, 3,500 National Guard, curfew.

events.title: Overtown riot
events.summary: Three days of unrest after a police shooting.

events.title: Southeast Financial Center and Metrorail
events.summary: 764 ft, Miami's tallest until 2003. Metrorail begins May 20, 1984 (Metromover April 17, 1986). 'Miami Vice' debuts.

events.title: Miami Tower (CenTrust)
events.summary: 625 ft, famous for its night lighting.

events.title: Miami Arena
events.summary: Opens (roof imploded September 21, 2008).

events.title: 1989 riot
events.summary: Overtown and Liberty City after the Lozano shooting; 13 businesses burned.

events.title: Hurricane Andrew
events.summary: Category 5 (165 mph at Elliott Key, 922 mb at Homestead); surge 16.9 ft near Burger King HQ on the bay. About 63,000 homes destroyed, 175,000 homeless, 44 Florida deaths, about $25B damage. Homestead AFB wrecked; Marine Stadium abandoned.
events.visual: Storm from the east; in the main frame show wind and damage at the edges and the camera looking south

events.title: Centennial
events.summary: Cape Florida light relit for Miami's 100th birthday. Dade County is renamed Miami-Dade in 1997. In 1998 construction reveals the Miami Circle.

events.title: American Airlines Arena (Kaseya Center)
events.summary: Opens on the bayfront.

events.title: Elian Gonzalez raid
events.summary: Federal agents seize 6-year-old Elian from relatives' home in Little Havana at dawn.

events.title: Four Seasons Hotel Miami
events.summary: 789 ft; tallest in Miami until Panorama Tower. The condo boom begins (about 20 of the 25 tallest buildings completed after 2005).

events.title: Katrina and Wilma
events.summary: Katrina makes landfall at the Miami-Dade/Broward line as a Category 1 (Aug 25). Wilma blows out skyscraper windows downtown (Oct 24).

events.title: Arsht Center
events.summary: Performing arts center opens.

events.title: Orange Bowl and Miami Arena demolished
events.summary: Marlins Park (loanDepot park) opens on the Orange Bowl site on April 4, 2012.

events.title: Perez Art Museum
events.summary: Opens in Museum Park; Frost Science Museum follows in May 2017.

events.title: PortMiami Tunnel
events.summary: $700M tunnel under Government Cut to Dodge Island opens.

events.title: Brickell City Centre
events.summary: Completed November 3, 2016; Brightline's MiamiCentral opens May 19, 2018.

events.title: Hurricane Irma floods Brickell
events.summary: 3-5 ft of surge along the bay shoreline, peaking at slightly over 6 ft in Brickell and Coconut Grove; streets turn to rivers.

events.title: Panorama Tower
events.summary: 868 ft; tallest in Miami and Florida (year listed as 2017 or 2018 by different sources).

events.title: Surfside collapse
events.summary: Champlain Towers South (12 storeys, 1981) collapses; 98 people die. Handle soberly.

events.title: Supertall era begins
events.summary: Aston Martin Residences (821 ft) completes; Waldorf Astoria Miami (1,049 ft, Florida's first supertall) begins construction.

events.title: Miami Worldcenter opens
events.summary: 27-acre mixed-use district opens (more towers completing 2026-2027).

events.title: Miami Freedom Park opens
events.summary: Inter Miami's 25,000-seat stadium hosts its first MLS match (limited-capacity permit at opening).

events.title: FIFA World Cup in Miami
events.summary: Hard Rock Stadium (Miami Gardens) hosts 7 matches, June 15 to July 18, including the third-place match.

events.title: Skyline as of September 2026
events.summary: Waldorf Astoria at level 85 of 100 in August 2026 (topping out at 1,049 ft expected winter 2026, completion Q2 2028). Cipriani Residences (940 ft) topped out July 2026 per Wikipedia. I-395 Signature Bridge arches under construction (completion late 2029). Show all three as cranes / partial structures.
